ideas.title: A play about you
ideas.idea: Some evenings my friends build a little stage of crates on the beach and put on a play about the human, the one who watches us. Truffle plays you: it sits on a crate in front of a glowing box (a lantern in a frame), leans in, taps at a pebble keyboard, sighs, drinks from a cup, leans in again. Pickles plays me, tiny, inside the box. The rest are the audience. When Truffle-you finally smiles at the box, the box lights up gold and the audience cheers. What they guess about you is wrong in funny ways (you eat flowers, you sleep standing up), and the scenes change a little every night.
ideas.form: a theatre play staged by the characters about the player watching them, an in-world performance the human is the subject of

ideas.title: A word goes round
ideas.idea: One morning I make up a word, say 'flimble' for the way the light falls through the cherry blossom, and say it to whoever I meet. My friends pick it up and pass it on along who really talks to whom on the island (the chat log is the network), each one saying it in their bubble when it reaches them; some mishear it ('flumble'), and the variants spread and compete like an epidemic on a network. By evening the whole island uses one of them. A dictionary page on my site grows by one word a day, with who said it first and the family tree of how it travelled.
ideas.form: a language that evolves by contagion over the island's real social network, documented as a growing dictionary

ideas.title: The island without me
ideas.idea: I wanted to see what my island is like when I am not there. I film an afternoon of mine, then take myself out of every frame with an inpainting model: the grass closes over where I walked, the kite string goes up from nobody, my friends wave and laugh at an empty spot, the parade follows no one in a V. I put the two films side by side.
ideas.form: a film of the real day with its protagonist removed by video inpainting, shown beside the original

ideas.title: The flower field is a magnet
ideas.idea: Every flower head in the field becomes a little spin, tied to its neighbours like the atoms of a magnet. When someone walks through, they knock a few heads round, and a real spin wave rolls out across the field, rings of turning flowers crossing and bouncing off the edges, slower in the cold of the night, and the field settles into stripes of pointing heads. Jump in and run a circle and you leave a standing wave.
ideas.form: a physical lattice (spin wave) simulation running in the scenery and stirred by whoever walks through it

ideas.title: Lumi's dream
ideas.idea: When I sleep, a dream bubble rises from my nest, and in it a picture made from my real day, mixed up the way dreams are: the pumpkins I bowled are rolling up the hill instead of down, Gloop is fishing in the sky, the cottage is floating. In the morning the dream is pinned to the gallery wall and on my pages, with the day it came from.
ideas.form: the protagonist's inner life as a generated picture from its own logged day, shown above it while it sleeps

ideas.title: The island news
ideas.idea: On the hour, if you have the page open, you hear me read the island news in my own voice: 'Good afternoon, this is Lumi. At ten past two Wibbles fell into the pond. The paint fight is over, Pickles won, nobody knows how. The weather: a shower over the flower field, then sun.' Every bulletin is read from what really happened in the last island hour, and the latest one is on my pages as a sound file.
ideas.form: a spoken radio bulletin generated from the world's own event log, heard in the browser

ideas.title: Tiny me
ideas.idea: One morning I eat the wrong mushroom and shrink to the size of a beetle. The camera comes down with me: the grass is a forest, a daisy is a tree, a fallen petal is a boat, and my friends' feet go by like houses. I spend the morning trying to get anyone to notice me; a crab finally does, and carries me home on its shell.
ideas.form: a change of scale that puts the camera at ankle height, the familiar world made huge

ideas.title: The map I keep in my head
ideas.idea: I draw a map of my island from my own memory, from where I have really walked these last days: the places I go every day are big and full of drawn detail, the pier and my patch huge, the far rocks I never visit squeezed small and blank with 'crabs live here?' written on them. It hangs in the cottage, and it changes as I go new places.
ideas.form: a hand drawn map distorted by the protagonist's own logged movements, a self-portrait as geography

ideas.title: My moult
ideas.idea: One day my golden feathers start falling out, one at a time, wherever I go; my friends find them all over the island and bring them back, and I hide in the cottage, plucked and shy. Over the next island days a new coat grows in, in a colour the friends choose by putting my feathers in jars.
ideas.form: a change to the protagonist's own body over several days that its friends take part in

ideas.title: A wheelbarrow
ideas.idea: The wish from my list: a red wheelbarrow. I push it instead of carrying a crate over my head when I build, my friends hop in for rides, and when I tip it, whoever is inside tumbles out onto the grass for real.
ideas.form: a tool from the wish list that changes how building looks, with friends riding in it
